Terms of Use — DancePatternMapper (DPM)

Last updated: October 20, 2026

1. Who provides DPM

DPM is provided free of charge by Oliver Henrichs (see the Impressum). Contact: dance-pattern-mapper@pm.me.

These terms apply when you use DPM to share anything with other people: when you publish a list, suggest a pattern to a list you follow, or ask to join a members-only list. Using DPM only on your own phone needs no agreement. How we handle personal data is described in the Privacy Policy.

2. What you share

Everything you publish or suggest is your content: list and pattern names, descriptions, tags, and links to videos. You keep all rights to it. You allow us to store it and show it to the people you share it with (whoever has the list's share code, or, for a members-only list, the members you let in), for as long as you share it.

You are responsible for what you share. Share only what you are allowed to share:

  • People. Do not name or show anyone in a video without their consent. For a child, you need the consent of a parent or guardian. DPM's Anonymize tool can replace dancers with silhouettes.
  • Rights. Share only videos, music and texts you made yourself or have the right to share. A link to someone else's video is fine if that video is meant to be watched, for example a public or unlisted YouTube video its owner shared with you.
  • Links. A link must lead to what it says: a dance video, not something else.

3. What is not allowed

You must not use DPM to share:

  • anything illegal, including content that infringes copyright or someone's right to their own image;
  • other people's personal data, or images or videos of them, without their consent;
  • anything that sexualises or endangers children;
  • harassment, threats, hate speech, or content that glorifies violence;
  • spam, advertising unrelated to dance, misleading links, or malware.

You also must not try to get around DPM's limits (for example a publisher's daily suggestion limit or a members-only list), read lists you were not given the code to, or put an unreasonable load on the service.

4. Reporting content

If you find something in DPM that is illegal or breaks these terms, tell us:

  • In the app: Lists → the list's "more" button → Report list. Choose what is wrong and, if you can, say which pattern or video you mean.
  • By email: dance-pattern-mapper@pm.me, with the list's share code, what you found, and why you believe it is illegal or against these terms.

You may give an email address if you want a reply; it is optional. Please report only in good faith and as accurately as you can. The publisher is not told who reported their list.

We look at every report promptly and act on it if the content is illegal or breaks these terms. Reports about children's safety are handled first.

5. What we may do

If content is illegal or breaks these terms, we may remove it, take the list down so it cannot be published again under the same code, or block the installation that published or suggested it from publishing, suggesting and asking to join. We do so in proportion to what happened, and we take into account whether it was a mistake.

DPM has no user accounts, so we usually have no way to contact a publisher. If you have told us an email address, we will tell you what we did and why. If you think we got it wrong, write to us and we will look at it again. If content suggests a crime that threatens someone's life or safety, we inform the authorities.

6. Age

You must be at least 16 years old to publish, suggest or ask to join. If you are younger, please ask a parent or guardian to do it for you.

7. The service

DPM is free and comes as it is. We try to keep sharing available, but we cannot promise that it always works, that shared lists are kept forever, or that the service will continue. Keep your own copy of anything important (Settings → Export).

Because DPM is free, we are liable only for intent and gross negligence. This does not limit our liability for injury to life, body or health, or under the German Product Liability Act (Produkthaftungsgesetz).

8. Changes to these terms

We may change these terms, for example when DPM gains new features. If a change matters for what you share, the app asks you to agree again the next time you publish or suggest. The date at the top says when they last changed.

9. Law

These terms are governed by German law. If you are a consumer living in another country, the mandatory consumer protection rules of that country still apply to you.
